title: Saskatchewan Opens Final 2026 Intake With 550 Permanent Residence Spots for Employers
excerpt: The province's last capped-sector intake of the year offers employers in retail, trucking, accommodation, and food services a narrow window on September 14-15 to nominate foreign workers for permanent residence.
body:
• Saskatchewan has allocated 550 permanent residence nomination spots across four capped sectors for its final intake of 2026, opening September 14-15.
  • Retail and food services each receive 175 spots, trucking gets 150, and accommodation receives 50 — all distributed on a first-come, first-served basis.
  • Only employers with workers whose work permits expire within six months can apply, and the November intake originally planned has been cancelled.
  • The province has already issued 2,628 of its 4,761 nominations for 2026, with previous intake windows filling within hours of opening.

Saskatchewan has earmarked 550 provincial immigration spaces for its final capped-sector intake of 2026, giving employers in retail, trucking, accommodation, and food services one last chance this year to put their foreign workers on a path to permanent residence.

The Saskatchewan Immigrant Nominee Program announced the allocation on September 2, confirming that the intake windows will open on September 14 and 15. The province simultaneously cancelled a planned November 2 intake, consolidating remaining nomination spaces into the September round, according to CIC News.

How the 550 Spots Break Down

The allocation is split across four capped sectors with staggered opening times. Retail, trade, and other services will open at 9:30 a.m. on September 14 with 175 spots. Trucking opens at the same time with 150 positions. Accommodation follows at 1:30 p.m. on September 14 with 50 spots, and food services opens at 1:30 p.m. on September 15 with 175 positions.

https://x.com/canadavisa_com/status/2095624174190657620

All spots will be distributed on a first-come, first-served basis. Employers must submit an Employer Position Assessment application once the intake opens, and applications submitted outside the designated intake period will be returned without processing.

Eligibility Requirements

Employers face strict eligibility criteria. They can only submit an EPA for workers whose work permits have six months or less remaining. Each EPA can include up to three positions for capped sectors, and each position listed counts toward the sector's cap.

Workers have 10 calendar days to review and confirm their employer's EPA submission after it is filed, followed by 60 days to submit their nomination application once conditional approval is granted. Processing times for EPA assessments have ranged from three to four weeks in 2026, according to SINP data.

"Nomination spaces previously allocated for later intakes will be made available in September."

— Saskatchewan Immigrant Nominee Program, September 2 update

Previous Intakes Filled Rapidly

The urgency for applicants is real. While the SINP notes that each intake window "may remain open for several days," spots for most sectors have historically been filled within hours of opening. The province has already filled 1,262 capped sector positions across its January through July intakes this year.

Saskatchewan's total nomination allocation for 2026 stands at 4,761. As of June 30, the province had issued 2,628 nominations — roughly 55% of its annual quota. The allocation is distributed across three tiers: priority sectors receive 2,380 spaces, capped sectors get 1,190, and other sectors are allotted 1,191.

What It Means for Foreign Workers in Saskatchewan

For the thousands of Indian and South Asian temporary foreign workers employed in Saskatchewan's retail, trucking, and food services industries, this intake represents a critical deadline. Missing it means waiting until 2027 for the caps to reset, or exploring alternative federal or provincial immigration pathways.

The SINP advises employers to complete their EPA applications in advance and be ready to submit the moment their sector's intake window opens. Given the history of rapid cap closures, preparation is essential.

Saskatchewan has identified seven priority sectors for 2026 — healthcare, agriculture, skilled trades, mining, manufacturing, energy, and technology — which together accounted for 1,466 nominations as of June 30. Workers in non-capped sectors face no intake restrictions and can submit applications at any time.
